newsitem.title: USA: Part of Florida teen's arm sliced off by road sign.
newsitem.headline: Part of Florida teen's arm sliced off by road sign.

text.p: A teenager's right arm was sliced off below the elbow when he stuck it out a car window and it hit a street sign, police said on Monday .

The 18-year-old was riding in a car driven by a friend though Oakland Park Sunday morning when he indicated he wanted to get out, the friend told police. The teen pointed out the window but hit an "End School Zone" sign that sheared off his right arm below the elbow.
The limb was found by rescuers 200 feet (66 metres) away.

The injured passenger was taken to the North Broward Medical Centre, where surgeons were trying to reattach the arm. A hospital spokesman on Monday named him as Nestor Hernandez Diaz and said he was a recent high school graduate.
The teenager "has improved today and is in a serious but stable condition," the spokesman said. He declined to give further details at the family's request.
